'''Marek Gaździcki''' (born 9 June 1956) is a [[Polish people|Polish]] [[high energy physics|high-energy]] [[nuclear physicist]], and the initiator and spokesperson of the [[NA61/SHINE|NA61/SHINE experiment]] at the [[CERN]] [[Super Proton Synchrotron]] (SPS).<ref name=na61proposal />

He, along with [[Mark I. Gorenstein]], predicted the threshold energy of the [[quark–gluon plasma]] production (the so-called "[[onset of deconfinement]]") in high energy [[heavy ion|nucleus-nucleus]] collisions.<ref name=smes /> These predictions have been confirmed by the [[NA49 experiment]] at the CERN SPS within the energy scan programme which was started by him and [[Peter Seyboth]].<ref name=evidence />

== Biography ==
Gaździcki was born on 9 June 1956 in [[Warsaw]], Poland, as the son of Teresa and Jerzy Gaździcki.  Living with his parents and his younger brother Pawel in Warsaw, he went to primary school in 1964 and graduated from high school in 1976. He studied physics at the [[Warsaw University]] from 1976 to 1980. After completing his first scientific degree, he married [[Maria Magdalena Klink]], a computer scientist, who graduated from the Warsaw University of Technology.

In the time from 1981 to 1984 he moved to Russia, where he became a researcher at the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in [[Dubna]]. Back in Poland, he received his PhD in [[Physics]], and became a lecturer at the Warsaw University in the time from 1989 to 1992. Additionally, he worked as a researcher at the [[University of Heidelberg]] (1986–1988) and at the [[University of Frankfurt/Main]].

Since 1992 he has been continuing studies as a Scientific Associate at the University of Frankfurt/M and from 2000 to 2001 at [[CERN]], in [[Geneva]], Switzerland. Since 2003, he holds a professorship at the [[Jan Kochanowski University]] in [[Kielce]], Poland, and works as researcher and outside lecturer at the University of Frankfurt/Main. In 2004 he became spokesperson of the Virtual Institute of the [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres]]: "Physics of Strongly Interacting Matter at High Densities" and in 2007 spokesperson of the [[NA61/SHINE]] experiment at the CERN SPS.

Marek Gaździcki currently lives with his wife and three children in the area of Frankfurt/M, Germany.

== Research ==
The most significant subjects investigated by Gaździcki are:

*1980–1986: Nucleus-nucleus interactions at 4.5''A''&nbsp;GeV (Dubna and Warsaw)
*1986–1992: Collisions of light nuclei at 20''A''&nbsp;GeV (Frankfurt/Main, Heidelberg and Warsaw)
*1992–1996: Pb+Pb collisions at 158''A''&nbsp;GeV (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)
*1994–1999: Predictions of the threshold for quark–gluon plasma production (Frankfurt/Main)
*1997–2007: Evidence for the threshold at the low SPS energies (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)
*since 1999: Low cross-section phenomena in Pb+Pb collisions at 158''A''&nbsp;GeV (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)
*1990–1993: [[STAR experiment]] at the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] (RHIC) (Warsaw and Frankfurt/Main)
*since 1992: Event-by-event fluctuations and the [[ALICE experiment]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC) (Warsaw, Frankfurt/Main and CERN)
*since 1998: [[Quarkonium]] production and high ''p''<sub>T</sub> phenomena (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)
*since 2003: [[NA61/SHINE|NA61/SHINE experiment]] at the [[CERN]] SPS (Frankfurt/Main and Kielce)

Selected achievements of Gaździcki's work are described as follows:

'''1980–1986: Nucleus-nucleus interactions at 4.5''A''&nbsp;GeV (Dubna and Warsaw)'''

Starting in 1980, Gaździcki participated in the [[SKM200 experiment]] at the [[Dubna Synchrophasotron]], focusing on the investigation of hadron production in ([[Helium|He]]&ndash;[[Magnesium|Mg]])+([[Lithium|Li]]&ndash;[[Lead|Pb]]) collisions at 4.5''A''&nbsp;GeV using a streamer chamber. The main results – which constituted the basis for his PhD thesis – were the first measurements of [[strangeness|strange]] [[hadron]] production in relativistic nucleus–nucleus collisions and a first observation of strange hadron yield enhancement in central ''A''+''A'' collisions.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=M.Kh. Anikina|year=1984
 |title=Characteristics of Lambda and K<sup>0</sup> particles produced in central nucleus–nucleus collisions at a 4.5&nbsp;GeV/''c'' momentum per incident nucleon
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=1313959
 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=25 |issue=1
 |pages=1–11
 |doi=10.1007/BF01571951
|bibcode = 1984ZPhyC..25....1A |s2cid=121294598
 |display-authors=etal|url-access=subscription
 }}</ref>

'''1986–1992: Collisions of light nuclei at 200''A'' GeV (Frankfurt/Main, Heidelberg and Warsaw)'''

Subsequently, (1986–1992) he took part in the [[NA35 experiment]] at the CERN SPS, where he studied hadron production in ({{SimpleNuclide|link=yes|Oxygen|16}}, {{SimpleNuclide|link=yes|Sulfur|32}})+([[Sulfur|S]]&ndash;[[Lead|Pb]]) collisions at 200''A'' GeV using a large volume streamer chamber. Here, a first observation of the enhancement of strange hadron production in ''A''+''A'' collisions at the SPS energies constituted the cardinal outcome of this experiment.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=J. Bartke ''et al.'' ([[NA35 experiment|NA35 Collaboration]])
 |year=1990
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=2350696
 |title=Neutral strange particle production in sulphur–sulphur and proton–sulphur collisions at 200&nbsp;GeV/nucleon
 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=48 |issue=2
 |pages=191–200
 |doi=10.1007/BF01554465
|s2cid=120308674
 |url-access=subscription
 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=T. Alber ''et al.'' ([[NA35 experiment|NA35 Collaboration]])
 |year=1994
 |title=Strange particle production in nuclear collisions at 200&nbsp;GeV per nucleon
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=2350696
 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=64 |issue=2
 |pages=195–207
 |doi=10.1007/BF01557391
|bibcode = 1994ZPhyC..64..195A |s2cid=124300126
 |url-access=subscription
 }}</ref> This result constituted the main part of Gazdzicki's habilitation.

'''1992–1996: Pb+Pb collisions at 158''A'' GeV (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)'''

In 1992, Gaździcki began working on the [[NA49 experiment]], which was based on [[time projection chamber]]s, the [[time of flight detector]]s and [[calorimeter]]s. The study of central Pb+Pb collisions at the top SPS energy confirmed the main result from the study of S+S interactions: the enhancement of [[strangeness production|strange hadron production]] in nucleus–nucleus collisions.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=P.G. Jones ''et al.'' ([[NA49 experiment|NA49 Collaboration]])
 |year=1996
 |title=Hadron yields and hadron spectra from the NA49 experiment
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=4019792
 |journal=[[Nuclear Physics A]]
 |volume=610 |pages=188c–199c
 |doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(96)00354-5
 |bibcode = 1996NuPhA.610..188J|url-access=subscription
 }}</ref>

'''1994–1999: Predictions of the threshold for quark–gluon plasma production (Frankfurt/Main)'''

Gaździcki's further work (1994–1999) was focused on the compilation, analysis and the interpretation of experimental results on system size and energy dependence of pion and strangeness production in A+A collisions, as well as the development of statistical models of strong interactions. Based upon these testings, Gaździcki observed the anomaly in energy dependence of pion and strange hadron yields in A+A collisions.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=M. Gaździcki |author2=D. Roehrich |year=1995
 |title=Pion multiplicity in nuclear collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=3196739
 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=65 |issue=2 |pages=215–223
 |doi=10.1007/BF01571878
|bibcode = 1995ZPhyC..65..215G |s2cid=122831487 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=M. Gaździcki |author2=D. Rohrich |year=1996
 |title=Strangeness in nuclear collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=3378594
 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=71 |issue=1996 |pages=55–64
 |doi=10.1007/s002880050147
 |arxiv=hep-ex/9607004
|citeseerx=10.1.1.340.7320 }}</ref>

Furthermore, he suggested that this anomaly is due to the transition to [[deconfinement]] matter occurring between top AGS (15''A'' GeV) and top SPS (158''A'' GeV) energies.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=M. Gaździcki
 |year=1995
 |title=Entropy in nuclear collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=3306054

 |volume=66 |issue=4
 |pages=659–662
 |doi=10.1007/BF01579641
|bibcode = 1995ZPhyC..66..659G |s2cid=122949215
 |url-access=subscription
 }}</ref> Lastly, along with Mark Gorenstein, he formulated the statistical model of the early stage which is a basis for the quantitative description of the observed effects,<ref name=smes>
{{cite journal
 |author1=M. Gaździcki |author2=M.I. Gorenstein |year=1999
 |title=On the early stage of nucleus–nucleus collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?eprint=hep-ph/9803462
 |journal=[[Acta Physica Polonica B]]
 |volume=30 |issue=9 |page=2705
 |arxiv=hep-ph/9803462
|bibcode = 1999AcPPB..30.2705G }}. Also available on the [http://th-www.if.uj.edu.pl/acta/vol30/abs/v30p2705.htm Acta Physica Polonica B website]</ref> and further predictions concerning the threshold for the [[quark–gluon plasma]] production.<ref>

 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2003.06.043

|bibcode = 2003PhLB..567..175G |s2cid=18103974 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal

'''1997-2007: Evidence for the threshold at the low SPS energies (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)'''

Based upon these results in 1997 Gaździcki, together with Peter Seyboth, initiated the energy scan with Pb+Pb collisions at the CERN SPS which was performed by NA49 from 1998 to 2002. The main results of this programme are: the observation of the onset of the steepening of energy dependence of pion yield at about 30''A'' GeV (''kink''), the observation of the non-monotonic energy dependence of positively charged kaon to pion ratio with the maximum located close to 30''A'' GeV (''horn''), and the observation of the anomaly in energy dependence of the transverse mass spectra of kaons (''step'') located in the SPS energy range.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=S.V. Afanasev ''et al.'' ([[NA49 experiment|NA49 Collaboration]])
 |year=2002
 |title=Energy dependence of pion and kaon production in central Pb+Pb collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=4921909
 |journal=[[Physical Review C]]
 |volume=66 |issue=5
 |article-number=054902
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.66.054902
 |arxiv=nucl-ex/0205002
|bibcode = 2002PhRvC..66e4902A |s2cid=6890591
 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=M. Gaździcki ''et al.'' ([[NA49 experiment|NA49 Collaboration]])
 |year=2004
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=5824389
 |title=Report from NA49
 |journal=[[Journal of Physics G]]
 |volume=30 |issue=8
 |pages=S701–S708
 |doi=10.1088/0954-3899/30/8/008
 |arxiv=nucl-ex/0403023
|bibcode = 2004JPhG...30S.701G |s2cid=119197566
 }}</ref> These observations serve as evidence for the [[onset of deconfinement]] at the CERN SPS energies.<ref name=evidence >
{{cite journal
 |author=C. Alt ''et al'' ([[NA49 experiment|NA49 Collaboration]])
 |year=2008
 |title=Pion and kaon production in central Pb+Pb collisions at 20''A'' and 30''A''&nbsp;GeV: Evidence for the onset of deconfinement

 |journal=[[Physical Review C]]
 |volume=77 |issue=2
 |article-number=024903
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.77.024903
 |arxiv=0710.0118
|bibcode = 2008PhRvC..77b4903A |s2cid=118390736
 }}</ref>

'''Since 1992: Event-by-event fluctuations (Warsaw, Frankfurt/Main and CERN)'''

In 1992 he started along with his collaborators the work on the development of statistical methods for the study of event-by-event fluctuations, as well as the study of physics of event-by-event fluctuations in A+A collisions. The most important results are the introduction of the commonly used measure of event-by-event fluctuations,<ref>

 |journal=[[Zeitschrift für Physik C]]
 |volume=54|issue=1 |pages=127–132
 |doi=10.1007/BF01881715
|bibcode = 1992ZPhyC..54..127G |s2cid=119688754 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author=M. Gaździcki
 |year=1999
 |title=A method to study chemical equilibration in nucleus–nucleus collisions
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=3670686
 |journal=[[European Physical Journal C]]
 |volume=8 |issue=1
 |pages=131–133
 |doi=10.1007/s100529901070
 |arxiv=nucl-th/9712050
|bibcode = 1999EPJC....8..131G |citeseerx=10.1.1.265.2925
 |s2cid=15610775
 }}</ref> and the cumulative variable for the correlation/fluctuation study,<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=A. Białas |author2=M. Gaździcki |year=1990
 |title=A new variable to study intermittency
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?j=PHLTA,B252,483
 |journal=[[Physics Letters B]]
 |volume=252 |issue=3 |pages=483–486
 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(90)90575-Q
 |bibcode=1990PhLB..252..483B
}}</ref> as well as the study of fluctuations and statistical models with conserved quantities.<ref>
{{cite journal

 |title=Particle number fluctuations in canonical ensemble
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=5853770
 |journal=[[Physical Review C]]
 |volume=70 |issue=3 |article-number=034901
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.70.034901

|bibcode = 2004PhRvC..70c4901B |s2cid=14400692 }}</ref>

'''Since 1998: Quarkonium production and high ''p''<sub>T</sub> phenomena (CERN and Frankfurt/Main)'''

Since 1998, Gaździcki, together with Mark Gorenstein, has been aiming at the compilation and interpretation of the data on the production of high (transverse) mass mesons, and at the development of the statistical model of strong interactions for high (transverse) mass domain. As a result, they discovered the independence of the {{Subatomic particle|J/Psi}} to the pion ratio of the system size in ''A''+''A'' collisions at 158''A''&nbsp;GeV.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=M. Gaździcki |author2=M.I. Gorenstein |year=1999
 |title=Evidence for statistical production of {{Subatomic particle|J/Psi}} mesons in nuclear collisions at the CERN SPS
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=4076036
 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]
 |volume=83 |issue=20 |pages=4009–4012
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.4009
 |arxiv=hep-ph/9905515
|bibcode=1999PhRvL..83.4009G
|s2cid=17525056 }}</ref> Moreover, they formulated the hypothesis of the statistical production of {{Subatomic particle|J/Psi}} mesons, and they found the ''m''<sub>T</sub> power-law scaling in high ''m''<sub>T</sub> domain in proton-proton interactions at high energies.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=M. Gaździcki |author2=M.I. Gorenstein |year=2001
 |title=Power law in hadron production
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=4579933
 |journal=[[Physics Letters B]]
 |volume=517 |issue=3–4 |pages=250–254
 |doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(01)01013-9
 |arxiv=hep-ph/0103010
|bibcode = 2001PhLB..517..250G |s2cid=5777137 }}</ref> Conclusively, the statistical interpretation of the scaling was formulated.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=V.V. Begun |author2=M. Gaździcki |author3=M.I. Gorenstein |year=2008
 |title=Power law in micro-canonical ensemble with scaling volume fluctuations
 |url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/spires/find/hep/www?irn=7713967
 |journal=[[Physical Review C]]
 |volume=78 |issue=2 |article-number=024904
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.78.024904
 |arxiv=0804.0075
|bibcode = 2008PhRvC..78b4904B |s2cid=118397460 }}</ref>

'''Since 2003: NA61/SHINE experiment at the CERN SPS (Frankfurt/Main and Kielce)'''

Motivated by the discovery of the threshold of the quark–gluon plasma production in 2003 Gaździcki initiated and became spokesperson of the [[NA61/SHINE]] experiment. The principal goals of this experiment are: the search of the critical point of strongly interacting matter, the study of the properties of the [[onset of deconfinement]] in nucleus-nucleus collisions and precision measurements of hadron production in nuclear interactions for neutrino ([[T2K]]) and cosmic-ray ([[Pierre Auger Observatory]] and [[KASCADE]]) experiments.<ref name=na61proposal>
{{Cite book
 |author=M. Gaździcki, Z. Fodor, G. Vesztergombi ([[NA61 experiment|NA61 Collaboration]])
 |year=2006
 |url=http://cdsweb.cern.ch/record/995681?ln=en
 |title=Study of hadron production in hadron–nucleus and nucleus–nucleus collisions at the CERN SPS
 |website=SPSC-P-330, CERN-SPSC-2006-034
|series=Proposal
 }}</ref>
